text.content:
The core conflict-resolution mechanic of Mind's Eye Theatre. Whenever roleplaying alone cannot settle a dispute between characters (or between a character and the world), the participants resolve it with a challenge: a Rock-Paper-Scissors test backed by Traits.

Initial Bid

  • The challenger states the conditions of the challenge (e.g., attacking, using a Discipline) and bids one Trait appropriate to the category involved (Physical, Social, or Mental).
  • The defender may relent (automatically lose the challenge, suffering no Trait loss) or match with a Trait of her own from the same category.
  • Once both sides have bid, they immediately test.

The Test

Both players throw Rock-Paper-Scissors simultaneously. Rock beats Scissors, Scissors beats Paper, Paper beats Rock; identical throws tie. The loser of a resolved test loses the Trait she bid for the rest of the session.

Ties

On a tie, each player declares how many Traits they currently have available in the category used. The player with fewer Traits loses the challenge (and the bid Trait). Players may understate (but never overstate) their total. Equal declared totals result in a draw, and both lose their bid Traits.

Overbidding

After losing a test, the loser may call for an overbid by risking a new Trait. Both sides then reveal their total Traits in the category, starting with whoever called the overbid. If the overbidder has at least double her opponent's total, a new test is made. This lets powerful elders eventually triumph over weaker but luckier opponents.

Negative Traits

During the initial bid, a player may call out a Negative Trait she believes her opponent possesses, forcing the opponent to bid an extra Trait if correct. If incorrect, the accuser must bid the extra Trait instead. Multiple Negative Traits may be called, each affecting the bid separately.

Static Challenges and Simple Tests

  • Static Challenge: A challenge against a Narrator representing a non-player obstacle (a lock, a feat of skill). The Narrator sets a difficulty (a number of Traits) that stands in for an opponent's total in a tie.
  • Simple Test: A single Rock-Paper-Scissors throw against a Narrator with no Traits at risk, used to see whether something works at all (common with Disciplines). Normally a win or tie succeeds; some effects require an outright win.

Retests

Certain Traits (often Abilities) grant a retest, letting a character discard a test result and try again. Multiple retests are allowed on one challenge, but each must come from a different source. Retests can be blocked by an opponent who can match the retest's conditions (e.g., Dodge blocking a Firearms retest).

Relenting

A player may relent at any point before the test occurs, automatically losing the challenge but risking no Traits.

Bonus Traits

Weapons and certain powers grant bonus Traits that count toward a character's total when ties are compared, but cannot be used as the initial bid itself.

Order of Challenges

When several challenges occur in the same turn, characters compare the number of Traits relevant to the action (Physical for a punch, Mental for a spell, etc.) to determine who acts first; higher totals act first, and actions without a Trait test resolve last. A character with fewer Traits who chooses to counter a faster attacker resolves simultaneously but uses up her action doing so.

Mob Challenges

When one character is challenged by multiple opponents (up to five at once), each attacker bids normally; the defender must bid enough Traits to cover every attacker or relent to some of them. All remaining participants then test simultaneously, and the defender's single throw is compared against each attacker's throw individually. The defender may only strike back at one attacker who lost to her, unless a special power grants multiple actions.
